title: Compact semantic recurrence is sufficient for G2
statement: A roughly one-million-parameter entity-attention plus GRU policy can score the complete legal option set, preserve public history and meet strict CPU reliability limits.
evidence_for: G1R provides a complete semantic option, compound action and recurrent lifecycle boundary; Orbit Wars solutions show small inference models can be strong when representation and rollout systems are efficient.
evidence_against: No neural model or CABT learning result exists in this repository.
next_test: Implement the model-facing projection and measure parameter count, permutation parity, gradients, CPU latency and complete-game reliability.

title: Recent replay intelligence will improve deck selection
statement: A version-pinned, bias-labeled seven-day replay sample will produce a more defensible deck shortlist and evaluation population than choosing from sample-agent decks alone.
evidence_for: The competition publishes daily episode datasets with exact deck submissions recoverable from valid replays.
evidence_against: Daily top episodes are selected and may not represent the full ladder; no current corpus has been transferred.
next_test: Verify the current manifests, execute the approved capped sample and report exact deck/archetype coverage with selection-bias warnings.

title: Strict recurrent PPO can reach anchor competence
statement: Terminal-reward recurrent PPO can exceed the strict G3b thresholds within five million non-forced choices per seed when trained against exact rule anchors and frozen policies.
evidence_for: The action space is legality-filtered and the fixed-deck specialist reduces the learning problem.
evidence_against: No PPO implementation or learning curve exists; public reports include PPO failures and collapse cases.
next_test: Only after G2 passes, run the preregistered three-seed G3a and G3b stages in private Kaggle notebooks.
